Tamil Christian Message | November Promise Message 2026 | Bro. Mohan C. Lazarus

Are you working hard for a better future but feeling worried about what lies ahead? Are you facing financial struggles, family problems, career challenges, or situations beyond your control? This November Promise Message 2026 is for you.

The Bible says in Proverbs 21:31, “The horse is prepared for the day of battle, But deliverance is of the LORD.” (NKJV)

Life teaches us to plan, prepare, and work hard. But no matter how carefully we plan, we cannot control every outcome. This verse reminds us that while preparation is our responsibility, true deliverance comes from the Lord.

You may have done everything possible to overcome a difficult situation, yet the answer may still seem far away. Do not lose hope. Your strength has limits, but God is not limited by your circumstances.

Do your best, prepare wisely, and trust God with the outcome. You don't have to let fear about tomorrow steal your peace today.

In this November Promise Message 2026, Bro. Mohan C. Lazarus shares an encouraging Tamil Christian Message to help you face life's challenges with renewed hope, courage, and trust in God.

Whether you are a believer or someone searching for hope, let this message remind you that you are not alone in your struggles. Step into November with faith, knowing that your future is not in your hands alone.

ISRO's journey has been one of India’s greatest scientific achievements. Built over decades with public money and the dedication of generations of scientists, the organisation has become a global symbol of indigenous innovation. But today, questions are being raised about its future as India’s space policy shifts manufacturing and commercial launch operations towards private companies. Reports of over 100 scientists leaving ISRO, concerns over the transfer of public infrastructure and technology to corporate players have added to the growing debate over whether India’s space programme is being quietly privatised.

In this episode of The Deshbhakt, we examine the changing role of ISRO and the implications of India’s new space policy. Is this a necessary step towards building a $44 billion space economy or are decades of publicly funded research and infrastructure being handed over to private corporations? Why are experienced scientists leaving the organisation? Can private companies take over commercial launches without weakening ISRO’s capabilities? And with India aiming for its own space station and a human mission to the Moon, are we putting the future of our space programme at risk?

James Talarico: Here Is How They Designed The System To Keep You Poor!

Is political corruption and extreme inequality pushing the working class to the breaking point? Representative James Talarico reveals the hidden systemic forces dismantling the American middle class and shares his radical blueprint to fix a rigged political system.

James Talarico is an 8th-generation Texan, former public school teacher, and current Democratic State Representative. As the potential first Democratic Senator elected in Texas since 1988, he campaigns on a progressive platform rooted in comprehensive political reform and unrigging the economy.

_This episode was recorded on September 8, 2026._

*In this episode, he explains:*
■ *The Rigged System:* Why the last 50 years of “trickle-down economics” is not an economic theory, but a deliberate theft designed to transfer wealth from the middle class to the ultra-rich.
■ *Crony Capitalism:* How monopolies in healthcare and lax campaign finance laws allow corporations to essentially purchase politicians, eliminating true competition and driving up prices for average citizens.
■ *The AI Threat:* Why leaving the development of artificial intelligence entirely to profit-driven billionaires threatens to create mass unemployment without any shared public benefits or worker protections.
■ *False Immigration Choices:* How politicians use extreme border rhetoric to divide voters, when the real solution requires simultaneous border security and clear, legal pathways to citizenship for undocumented residents.
■ *Systemic Overhaul:* Why simply electing new politicians changes nothing unless we first dismantle the corrupt incentive structures of gerrymandering, the two-party system, and unregulated corporate lobbying.

Is AI a bubble, or are we underestimating how much it can change? That’s the question I kept coming back to in San Francisco. Young companies are attracting extraordinary valuations, while I’m still trying to see how the promised productivity gains are reaching the wider economy.

I put that scepticism to Akshay Kothari of Notion, Vijay Krishnan of Turing, and Ricursive Intelligence’s Azalia Mirhoseini and Anna Goldie. We discuss where the money is coming from, how much of it is moving between AI companies, and what businesses and individuals will actually pay for. They make the case for capabilities that are already useful, smaller teams doing more, and benefits that take time to spread. We also get into chips, human work, AI risks and what India should build.

The technology can be powerful and the prices can still be wrong. I wanted to understand how to tell the difference.

We scan a QR code, enter a PIN, and move on. I wanted to understand everything that happens in between. If a payment feels instant and costs us nothing, who is doing the work, who is taking the risk, and who is paying for it?

I sat down with Sameer Nigam of PhonePe, Harshil Mathur of Razorpay, and Sohini Rajola of NPCI to follow a payment through the system. We draw out the journey between an app, the banks and NPCI, get into why the confirmation on our phone and the settlement between banks are different things, and compare that with what happens when we use a credit card. From rewards and merchant fees to fraud, failed transactions and the cost of handling cash, there is a business behind every way we choose to pay.

The conversation also gets into MDR, how the ecosystem funds itself, and what it takes to keep investing in wider access. Then we look ahead: cross-border payments, business payments, wearable rings, digital tipping, and AI agents that might eventually shop and pay for us. The guests disagree on how quickly that future arrives, especially in India.

If you were starting a payments business today, which problem would you try to solve? Watch the full conversation and tell me below.
